query: Port Solas electricity consumption on 2013-10-03 from 12:00 to 13:00: distinguish physical demand effects from monitoring and data-logging artifacts

evidence.claim: Port Solas retained electrical service during the regional event while carrying unusually high HVAC demand.
evidence.exact_quote: Despite the drastic current drop in adjacent external sectors, Port Solas experienced no service interruptions. All infrastructure remained stable, supporting the high 4x HVAC load demands recorded throughout the district during the current heat wave.

evidence.claim: A localized heat event began at noon on October 3 and immediately increased cooling-equipment use across the Port Solas grid.
evidence.exact_quote:
The event initiated at exactly 12:00:00 on October 3, 2013. 

System data indicates that the arrival of this localized heat at the specified time triggered an immediate and sharp spike in cooling equipment utilization across the grid.

evidence.claim: A scheduled monitoring-system upgrade suspended real-time reporting from 12:00 to 13:00 without interrupting physical electricity flow.
evidence.exact_quote:
Real-Time Reporting: Please be advised that the transmission of real-time usage reports to the central dashboard will be suspended for the duration of the upgrade (12:00:00 to 13:00:00). High-level monitoring will resume immediately upon successful installation.
- Power Stability: Grid Operations confirms that the physical flow of power remains constant during the upgrade period. No service interruptions or local outages will occur as a result of this software maintenance.

evidence.claim: The recorded electricity-consumption values were depressed by 40 percent from 12:00 to 13:00 because sub-meter packets were not aggregated, rather than because physical usage fell.
evidence.exact_quote: Analysis shows that the recorded electricity consumption values dropped accurately by 40 percent. This drop was observed even during periods of high demand, where load profiles should have remained consistent or plateaued at peak levels. The 40% reduction is determined to be a result of the software’s failure to aggregate sub-meter packets during the sync lag, rather than an actual drop in facility power usage.

impacts.rationale: The report explicitly quantifies a 40 percent recording reduction during this one-hour forecast interval and attributes it to failed packet aggregation, so the edit applies to the recorded target rather than latent electricity use.

Real-time reporting is scheduled to be suspended during the same interval while physical power flow remains constant, independently supporting an observation-layer disruption but providing no additional quantitative magnitude.

The heat event begins inside the forecast horizon and drives a sharp cooling-utilization spike while Port Solas maintains service. The reported 4x figure concerns HVAC load demands rather than total city electricity consumption, so it does not justify a numeric edit to the total target.
